prompt: What is an Increment? Choose the best answer.

options.text: The sum of all Product Backlog items completed during a Sprint
All items in the Sprint Backlog that could be released regardless of whether the Product Owner decides to actually do it
All Done items in the Sprint Backlog
An Increment is a concrete stepping stone toward the Product Goal.

explanation: Each Increment is additive to all prior Increments and must be usable to provide value.

prompt: Who must conform to the  Definition of Done? Choose the best answer.
explanation: The Developers are required to conform to the Definition of Done.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Definition of Done; Developers.

prompt: True or False: It is allowed to skip the Daily Scrum if there is nothing interesting to talk about?
explanation: Each event is a formal opportunity to inspect and adapt; skipping reduces transparency.

prompt: What belongs solely to the Developers of the Scrum Team? Choose the best answer.
explanation: The Sprint Backlog is a plan by and for the Developers.

prompt: Who participates in the Sprint Review? Select all that apply.
explanation: The Scrum Team and stakeholders collaborate on what was done and what to do next.

prompt: True or False: The Product Owner and the Scrum Master can actively work as Developers?
explanation: They may perform Developer work; if so, they participate as Developers in the Daily Scrum.

prompt: Select the two events in which people outside the Scrum Team are allowed to attend. Choose the best two answers.
explanation: Stakeholders attend Sprint Review; others may be invited to Sprint Planning for advice.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Sprint Review; Sprint Planning.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of an Increment? Choose the best answer.

options.text: A mock-up of the product marketing materials.
A plan for the overall product release.
A valuable, useful set of product features.

explanation: Only a valuable, usable set of features that meet the DoD forms an Increment.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Increment; Definition of Done.

prompt: What is the purpose of the Sprint Review? Choose the best answer.

options.text: To create a common understanding of progress toward the Sprint Goal and how progress is trending toward completing the work in the Sprint Backlog.
To create a common understanding of what can be delivered in the Increment and how will the work needed to deliver the Increment be achieved.
To create a list of improvements that the Scrum Team will implement in the next Sprint.
To inspect the outcome of the Sprint and determine future adaptations.

explanation: Participants inspect the Increment and adapt the Product Backlog for maximizing value.

prompt: Which topics are covered during Sprint Planning? Choose the best three answers.

options.text: What new technologies could be used to speed up the velocity of the Scrum Team?
What is the size of the Technical Debt and how it could be removed?
How will chosen work get done.
What can be done this Sprint?

explanation: Sprint Planning answers Why the Sprint is valuable, What can be done, and How the work will get done.

prompt: What is Scrum? Choose the best answer.

options.text: A software development methodology which is intended to improve software quality.
A sequential design process, used in software development processes, in which progress is seen as flowing steadily downwards.
A framework within which people can address complex adaptive problems, while delivering valuable products.

explanation: Scrum is a lightweight framework to generate value through adaptive solutions to complex problems.

prompt: What enhances the transparency of an Increment? Choose the best answer.

options.text: Keeping track of and estimating all undone work to be completed in a "hardening" Sprint.
Reporting Sprint progress to the stakeholders daily.
Updating Sprint tasks properly in the electronic tracking tool.
Doing all the work needed to meet the Definition of Done.

explanation: A shared DoD clarifies what ‘done’ means and makes the Increment transparent.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Definition of Done; Transparency.

prompt: What is the timebox for a Sprint Planning? Choose the best answer.

options.text: As much as it is necessary to make task breakdown and estimates for all items in the Sprint Backlog.

explanation: Maximum eight hours for a one-month Sprint; shorter Sprints are usually shorter.

prompt: True or False: The Daily Scrum timebox depends on the number of Developers on the Scrum Team.
explanation: Daily Scrum is always 15 minutes.

prompt: True or False: The Sprint Backlog is created at the Sprint Planning. It is prohibited to add new work into the Sprint Backlog later by the Developers.
explanation: The Sprint Backlog is updated throughout the Sprint as more is learned.

prompt: What is Product Backlog refinement? Choose the best two answers

options.text: Product Backlog refinement initiates the Sprint.
Product Backlog refinement is not allowed in Scrum. Everything needs to be clear before the first Sprint can start.
An ongoing activity to add details, such as description, order and size to Product Backlog items.
The act of breaking down and further defining Product Backlog items.

explanation: Refinement is ongoing and clarifies PBIs by adding details and breaking them down.

prompt: Which event initiates the Sprint? Choose the best answer.

options.text: Meeting with the PMO (Project Management Office)

explanation: Sprint Planning initiates the Sprint by laying out the work for the Sprint.

prompt: What are two characteristics of the Product Owner? Choose the best two answers.

options.text: Lead Scrum evangelist in the organization
Lead Facilitator of Key Stakeholder Involvement

explanation: PO maximizes value and understands the market for the product.

prompt: True or False: It is a good practice to have from time to time a special technical Sprint that consists only of tasks removing the technical debt without implementing any new functionality.
explanation: Each Sprint must produce a usable Increment of value.

prompt: True or False: Other people than the Scrum Team can attend the Sprint Planning in order to provide advice.
explanation: The Scrum Team may invite others to Sprint Planning to provide advice.

prompt: True or False: Scrum does not allow additional meetings that are not defined in Scrum.
explanation: Additional meetings are allowed if they help achieve Scrum Team goals.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Scrum framework (minimal, may wrap practices).

prompt: Who is responsible for crafting the Sprint Goal at the Sprint Planning? Choose the best answer.
explanation: The whole Scrum Team collaborates to define the Sprint Goal.

prompt: What is true about the ordering of items in the Product Backlog? Choose the best answer.What is the order of items in the Product Backlog? Choose the best answer.

options.text: The recently added items at the top
The less clear items at the top
Less valuable and most unclear items at the bottom

explanation: The PO orders to maximize value; clear, valuable items typically rise to the top.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Product Backlog (ordered list; PO accountable).

prompt: How does the Scrum Master serve the Product Owner? Choose the best three answers.

options.text: Leading and coaching the organization in its Scrum adoption
Helping find techniques for effective Product Goal definition and Product Backlog management.
Helping the Scrum Team understand the need for clear and concise Product Backlog items.
Facilitating stakeholder collaboration as requested or needed.

explanation: SM supports PO with backlog techniques, PBIs clarity, and stakeholder collaboration.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Scrum Master service to Product Owner.

prompt: What are two ways that regulatory compliance issues are dealt with in Scrum? Choose the best two answers.

options.text: They are addressed by a separate team. This team is responsible for all compliance issues.
They are added to the Product Backlog and addressed in early Sprints, while always requiring at least some business functionality, no matter how small.
They are addressed along with functional development of the product.
They are discussed, determined, and documented before actual feature development Sprints.

explanation: Address compliance via PBIs (prefer early) and as part of ongoing development; consider adding to DoD.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Product Backlog; Definition of Done (quality & criteria).

prompt: What is the purpose of the Sprint Retrospective? Choose the best answer.

options.text: To take time to judge the validity of the project.
It is a meeting where the Developers on the Scrum Team synchronizes activities and creates a plan for the next 24 hours
It is a meeting to inspect the Increment and adapt the Product Backlog if needed
The purpose of the Sprint Retrospective is to plan ways to increase quality and effectiveness.

explanation: Retrospective plans improvements to increase quality and effectiveness.

prompt: Which three behaviors demonstrate that a Scrum Team is self-managing? Choose the best three answers.

options.text: The Scrum Master is no longer needed.
The Scrum Team members are working within the boundaries of their functional description and nicely handing off work from analysts to developer to tester to integration.
Stakeholders are attending the Daily Scrum to check progress and work with the Scrum Master to optimize the functional scope for the Sprint.
The Scrum Team has all the skills needed to create an Increment.
Developers collaboratively selecting their own work during the Sprint.
The Developers create their own Sprint Backlog, reflecting all work that is part of the Definition of Done.

explanation: Self-managing teams decide who does what, when and how; they are cross-functional and own their plan.

prompt: True or False: Scrum recommends using only those Scrum components which  are most suited for a particular project.
explanation: Scrum exists only in its entirety; each element serves a specific purpose.

prompt: What does Product Backlog management include? Choose the best three answers.

options.text: Moving Product Backlog items into the Sprint Backlog
Presenting Product Backlog items to the Key Stakeholders
Ensuring that the Product Backlog is transparent, visible and understood.
Creating and clearly communicating Product Backlog items;
Developing and explicitly communicating the Product Goal

explanation: PO develops Product Goal, creates/communicates PBIs, orders them, and ensures transparency.

prompt: Who is responsible for the monitoring of the remaining work towards the Product Goal? Choose the best answer.

options.text: The Scrum Master and The Developers
The Product Owner and The Developers

explanation: The PO monitors progress toward the Product Goal and makes it transparent.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Product Owner (progress toward Product Goal).

prompt: What is the purpose of the Sprint Retrospective? Choose the best three answers.

options.text: To get technical or domain advice from specialists invited by the Developers or the Scrum Master
To get feedback from the Key Stakeholders invited by the Product Owner
To inspect how the last Sprint went with regards to individuals, interactions, processes and tools.
To identify the most impactful improvements to be addressed as soon as possible.
To inspect (and if necessary adapt) the Definition of Done.

explanation: Inspect last Sprint, adapt DoD if needed, and identify changes to improve effectiveness.

prompt: What are two effective ways for the Scrum Team to make non-functional requirements visible? Choose the best two answers.

options.text: Put them on a separate list on the Scrum Board, available for all to see.
Run the integration and regressions tests before the end of the Sprint, and capture the open work for the Sprint Backlog of the next Sprint.
Add them to the Product Backlog to ensure transparency.
Add them to the Definition of Done so the work is taken care of every Sprint.

explanation: Model NFRs as PBIs for transparency and/or include them in the DoD so they are met every Sprint.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Product Backlog; Definition of Done.

prompt: Which statements best describe the features of a Product Backlog? Choose the best three answers.

options.text: When the final version of a product is rolled out, its Product Backlog is dismissed
A Product Backlog could be closed when it contains no items to include in the next Sprint
It is an emergent and ordered list.
It is the single source of work undertaken by the Scrum Team.
As long as a product exists, its Product Backlog also exists

explanation: The Product Backlog is emergent, ordered, the single source of work, and exists as long as the product exists.

prompt: True or False: Only the Product Owner and the Developers participate in the Sprint Planning. There is nothing to do for the Scrum Master
explanation: The entire Scrum Team plans the Sprint; the SM ensures the event happens and is productive.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Sprint Planning; Scrum Master.

prompt: Bring the Scrum events in the right order (sort):

options.text: Sprint Planning, Daily Scrum, Sprint Review, Sprint Retrospective
Sprint Retrospective, Sprint Planning, Daily Scrum, Sprint Review
Sprint Retrospective, Daily Scrum, Sprint Review, Sprint Planning
Daily Scrum, Sprint Review, Sprint Retrospective, Stakeholder Meeting, Sprint Planning

explanation: Order is Planning → (many) Daily Scrums → Review → Retrospective within a Sprint.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Events sequence within a Sprint.

prompt: What are essential components of the Scrum Framework? Choose all that apply.
explanation: Scrum consists of Scrum Teams and their accountabilities, events, artifacts, and their commitments.

prompt: The Scrum Master does the following regarding the Daily Scrum. Choose all that apply.

options.text: The Scrum Master is responsible for conducting the Daily Scrum
The Scrum Master ensures that the Developers have the event
The Scrum Master teaches the Developers to keep the Daily Scrum within the 15-minute time-box
The Scrum Master ensures that only Developers participate in the Daily Scrum

explanation: Developers conduct the Daily Scrum; SM ensures it happens, is timeboxed, and is not disrupted.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Daily Scrum; Scrum Master service to the team.

prompt: What are the Scrum Artifacts? Choose all that apply.
explanation: Artifacts are Product Backlog, Sprint Backlog, and Increment (Sprint Goal is a commitment for Sprint Backlog).

prompt: How frequently should Scrum Users inspect Scrum artifacts and progress toward agreed goals? Choose the best answe

options.text: Frequently, but it should not get in the way of the work.

explanation: Inspect frequently and diligently without undermining delivery.

prompt: What are the characteristics of a Scrum Team? Choose the best three answers.

options.text: Having at least one test engineer among the Developers.
Having the Scrum Master as a part-time Developer in the Scrum Team.
A Scrum Team is self-managing, meaning they internally decide who does what, when and how.
Scrum Teams are cross-functional, meaning the members have all the skills necessary to create value each Sprint.
Within a Scrum Team, there are no sub-teams or hierarchies.

explanation: Scrum Teams are self-managing, cross-functional, and have no sub-teams/hierarchies.

prompt: True or False: All the Scrum Teams working on the same product should have the same Sprint length.
explanation: Sprint length is up to each team; alignment may be useful but is not required.

prompt: True or False: If an item in the Sprint Backlog cannot be finished by the end of the Sprint, the Sprint is cancelled.
explanation: A Sprint is cancelled only if the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete.

prompt: Who has the authority to cancel the Sprint? Choose the best answer.

options.text: The Product Owner and the Scrum Master

explanation: Only the Product Owner can cancel the Sprint.

prompt: What happens during the Sprint? Select the best three answers.

options.text: The Sprint Goal is changed frequently to reflect the status of the remaining work
Sprint scope is defined at the Sprint Planning and cannot be changed
Scope may be clarified and renegotiated with the Product Owner as more is learned
No changes are made that would endanger the Sprint Goal

explanation: No changes that endanger the Sprint Goal; quality does not decrease; scope may be clarified/re-negotiated with PO.

prompt: True or False: It is a good practice to have at least two Product Owners on big projects.
explanation: The Product Owner is one person, not a committee.

prompt: Who must participate in the Daily Scrum? Choose the best answer.

options.text: The Developers and the Scrum Master.
The Developers and the Product Owner.
The Scrum Master and the Product Owner.

explanation: The Daily Scrum is for the Developers.

prompt: Scrum is founded on…Choose the best two answers.
explanation: Scrum is founded on empiricism and lean thinking.

prompt: A Product Owner wants advice from the Scrum Master about estimating work in Scrum. What guidance should a Scrum Master give? Choose the best answer.

options.text: Product Backlog items must be estimated in story points.
Estimates must be in relative units.
Estimates are made by the Product Owner, but are best checked with the Developers.
Estimates are made by the people doing the work.

explanation: The people who will do the work provide the estimates.

prompt: True or False: The Scrum Master is focused primarily on the Scrum Team and usually does not care about those outside the Scrum Team.
explanation: Scrum Masters serve the Scrum Team and the larger organization.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Scrum Master (service to organization).

prompt: True or False: All Scrum Teams working on the same Product should use the same Product Backlog.
explanation: One Product Backlog per product.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Product Backlog (single source of work).

prompt: True or False: During each Sprint Retrospective the Scrum Team reviews the Definition of Done and changes it if necessary.
explanation: The team may adapt the DoD during the Retrospective.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Sprint Retrospective; Definition of Done.

prompt: Which of the following are topics for the Developers to discuss at the Daily Scrum as they inspect their progress toward the Sprint Goal? Choose the best three answers.

options.text: Will today's work negatively impact our ability to meet the Sprint Goal for the Sprint following this one?
What will I be working on tomorrow?
Are there any impediments blocking progress toward the Sprint Goal?
Are there any decisions that need to be made to maintain progress toward the Sprint Goal?
What have we learned since yesterday, and how should we modify our plan to increase our ability to meet the Sprint Goal?

explanation: Daily Scrum focuses on progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapting the plan for the next 24 hours.

prompt: Who can make changes to the Product Backlog? Choose the best two answers.

options.text: The Developers, when the responsibility has been delegated to them by the Product Owner

explanation: The PO manages the Product Backlog and may delegate work; others can change it only under PO’s authority.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Product Owner (backlog management, delegation).

prompt: Who participates in the Sprint Planning? Choose all the apply.
explanation: The Scrum Team plans the Sprint together.

prompt: How does the Scrum Master serve the Scrum Team? Choose the best three answers.

options.text: Adding or removing developers from the Scrum Team in accordance with team velocity changes
Helping the Developers as the team leader
Coaching the team members in self-management and cross-functionality.
Causing the removing of impediments to the Scrum Team's progress.
Ensuring that all Scrum events take place and are positive, productive, and kept within the timebox.

explanation: Coach self-management/cross-functionality, remove impediments, and ensure events happen and are healthy.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Scrum Master (service to team).

prompt: How does the Scrum Master serve the organization? Choose the best three answers.

options.text: Mixing experienced developers and junior specialists across different Scrum Teams in the organization to speed up Scrum adoption
Planning and advising Scrum implementation within the organization
Making sure the key stakeholders are invited on all Scrum Reviews within the organization
Removing barriers between stakeholders and Scrum Teams.
Leading , training and coaching the organization in its Scrum adoption.

explanation: SM leads/trains/coaches, plans/advises Scrum implementations, and removes barriers between stakeholders and teams.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Scrum Master (service to organization).

prompt: What is the Sprint Backlog composed of? Choose the best answer.

options.text: The Product Backlog items selected for this Sprint
The Product Backlog items selected for this Sprint plus a set of internal tasks identified by the Developers.
The Product Backlog items selected for this Sprint, the plan for delivering them and the Sprint Goal.

explanation: Sprint Goal (why), selected PBIs (what), and plan for delivering the Increment (how).

prompt: The Product Owner is not collaborating with the Developers during the Sprint. What are two valuable actions for a Scrum Master to take? Choose the best two answers.

options.text: Inform the Product Owner's functional manager.
Stop the Sprint and send the Product Owner to a course and restart.
Bring up the problem at the Sprint Retrospective.
Coach the Product Owner in the values of Scrum and incremental delivery.

explanation: Surface the issue at Retrospective and coach the PO to restore collaboration and transparency.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Scrum Master service to PO & team.

prompt: The Developers select a set of Product Backlog items for a Sprint Backlog with the intent to get the selected items done by the end of the Sprint. Which three phrases best describe the purpose of a Definition of Done? Choose the best three answers.

options.text: It tracks the percentage complete of a Product Backlog item.
It controls whether the Developers have performed their tasks.
It provides a template for elements the need to be included in the documentation.
It creates transparency over the work inspected at the Sprint Review.
It defines what it takes for an Increment to be ready for release.
It guides the Developers in creating a forecast at the Sprint Planning.

explanation: DoD defines ‘done’ (releasable), guides forecasting in planning, and makes inspected work transparent.

prompt: What could be the single source of work for any changes to be made to the product? Choose the best answer.
explanation: Product Backlog is the single source of work undertaken by the Scrum Team.

prompt: If one or more aspects of a process deviate outside acceptable limits when must an adjustment be made? Choose the best answer.

options.text: The deviations should be discussed at the Daily Scrum and then an adjustment must be made
After clarifying all the details with the Product Owner
As soon as possible to minimize further deviation

explanation: When a process or product is outside acceptable limits, adjust as soon as possible.

prompt: In which event are the Key Stakeholders allowed to participate? Choose the best answers.In which meeting are the Key Stakeholders allowed to participate? Choose the best answer.
explanation: Stakeholders participate in the Sprint Review.

prompt: What are the three pillars of empiricism that uphold Scrum? Choose the best three answers.
explanation: Transparency, inspection, and adaptation uphold empiricism.

prompt: Please select the correct timebox for each Scrum event.

options.text: Sprint Review, 3 hours or less, Daily Scrum, 15 minutes, Sprint Retrospective, 4 hours or less, Sprint Planning, 8 hours or less
Sprint Review, 8 hours or less, Daily Scrum, 15 minutes, Sprint Retrospective, 3 hours or less, Sprint Planning, 4 hours or less
Sprint Review, 4 hours or less, Daily Scrum, 15 minutes, Sprint Retrospective, 3 hours or less, Sprint Planning, 8 hours or less

explanation: Review ≤4h, Daily 15m, Retrospective ≤3h, Planning ≤8h (for a one-month Sprint).

prompt: What does a burndown chart show? Choose the best answer.

options.text: Hierarchy of tasks that comprise a project
The evolution of the amount of uncertainty during a project
Dependencies, start times and stop times for project tasks

explanation: Burndown charts visualize remaining work over time.
source: Common Scrum practice; not prescribed by the Guide.

prompt: True or False: It is normal to have a 'Hardening Sprint' to remove all Technical Debt and prepare the Product for upcoming release.
explanation: Each Sprint should produce a Done, usable Increment; ‘hardening Sprints’ indicate lack of built-in quality.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Increment; Definition of Done.

prompt: What are the formal Scrum events for inspection and adaptation? Choose all the apply.
explanation: Planning, Daily Scrums, Review, and Retrospective are the four formal inspect-and-adapt events (inside the Sprint).

prompt: What should be taken into account for the Definition of Done? Choose the best two answers.

options.text: Definition of Done of other Scrum Teams working on other products
Definition of Done of other Scrum Teams working on the same product

explanation: Use organizational standards as a minimum; share a DoD across teams working on the same product.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Definition of Done (organization & multi-team).

prompt: Could the Sprint Planning be finished if only work planned for the first days of the Sprint is decomposed to units of one day or less? Choose the best answer.

options.text: No, all items in the Sprint Backlog should be decomposed to units of one day or less by the end of the Sprint Planning
Yes, if the remaining work is also estimated, maybe in bigger units

explanation: Decompose enough to start; remaining details emerge during the Sprint.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Sprint Planning; Sprint Backlog (emergent).

prompt: What are the two essential features a Scrum Team should possess? Choose the best two answers.

options.text: It should use tools, processes and techniques approved by the Organization
It should be flexible enough to complete all the work planned for the Sprint even if some team members are on vacation
A Scrum Team is self-managing, meaning members internally decide who does what, when, and how.
A Scrum Team is cross-functional, meaning the members have all the skills necessary to create value each Sprint.

explanation: Self-managing and cross-functional are core characteristics of Scrum Teams.

prompt: A Scrum Team is a cohesive unit of professionals that consists of which of the following? Choose all that apply.
explanation: One Scrum Master, one Product Owner, and Developers.

prompt: True or False: The Definition of Done is created during the first Sprint and remains unchanged until the Product release.
explanation: The DoD may be adapted (e.g., during Retrospectives) as the team improves.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Definition of Done; Sprint Retrospective.

prompt: True or False: Scrum does not describe agile processes and techniques.
explanation: Scrum is not a process or technique; it is a framework that can contain practices.

prompt: Who is responsible for tracking the total work remaining in the Sprint Backlog to project the likelihood of achieving the Sprint Goal? Choose the best answer.

options.text: The Product Owner and the Developers

explanation: Developers inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the plan at the Daily Scrum.

prompt: What happens when a Sprint is cancelled? Choose the best answer.

options.text: At the Sprint Retrospective the Scrum Master determines who among the Developers is responsible for cancelling the Sprint.
Several top Product Backlog Items are taken into the Sprint Backlog to replace the obsolete items.
Product Backlog Items that do not meet the Definition of Done are returned to the Product Backlog for future consideration.

explanation: Done items may be reviewed; undone items return to the Product Backlog.

prompt: Which of the following are no timeboxed events in Scrum? Choose the best two answers.
explanation: Refinement is ongoing (not an event). Release Planning is optional and not prescribed in the Guide.

prompt: What does a Cone of Uncertainty show? Choose the best answer.

options.text: Hierarchy of tasks that comprise a project
Dependencies, start times and stop times for project tasks
How much work remains till the end of the Sprint
How much is known about the Product over time

explanation: It visualizes uncertainty decreasing (knowledge increasing) over time.

prompt: True or False: The Sprint Goal is a commitment by the Developers.
explanation: The Sprint Goal is the commitment for the Sprint Backlog, owned by the Developers.

prompt: Who is allowed to change the Sprint Backlog during the Sprint? Choose the best answer.

options.text: The Developers and the Product Owner

explanation: The Sprint Backlog is a plan by and for the Developers; they update it throughout the Sprint.

prompt: Who is accountable for managing the Product Backlog? Choose the best answer.
explanation: The Product Owner is the single person accountable for Product Backlog management.
